outcome: Find reproducible gameplay, compatibility, economy and regression defects earlier across builds, devices and network conditions — with replayable evidence attached
overview: Content and device matrices grow faster than QA headcount, so regressions escape into live builds, certification slips and engineers lose days reproducing defects they cannot pin down. This solution runs scripted and exploratory agents across approved test paths, device profiles and network conditions, captures deterministic replays and telemetry for every failure, and files triaged issues straight into the existing defect workflow and CI gates. Known-bad fixtures prove the harness actually detects the defects it claims to, and flaky tests are quarantined rather than ignored. A 6–10-week build pilot measures scenario coverage, reproduction time and escaped defects against the team’s current baseline. Reference builds are specified for AWS and Azure.

benefits.text: Increase meaningful scenario coverage across builds, devices and network conditions
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Coverage counts scenarios the team agrees are meaningful, not raw test counts; gains depend on deterministic hooks existing in the build

benefits.text: Reduce reproduction and triage time with deterministic replays, logs and telemetry per failure
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Replay fidelity depends on deterministic seeds and engine support; non-deterministic and physics-sensitive defects remain hard to reproduce

benefits.text: Cut escaped defects reaching certification and live players
benefits.source: Reference design capability, Redington Gaming catalogue
benefits.limits: Automation never substitutes for human gameplay QA; fun, feel and emergent design defects are outside what any harness can detect

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); builds, test assets, replays and defect evidence remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No build automation or reproducible build pipeline
notFor.why: Automated testing needs a build it can fetch, install and run on demand; without CI there is nothing to gate and nothing to run against

notFor.situation: No deterministic hooks or test harness in the game client
notFor.why: Without deterministic seeds and scriptable entry points, failures cannot be replayed and results cannot be trusted enough to gate a release

notFor.situation: A brief to replace the human QA team
notFor.why: The design targets reproducible defect classes and explicitly reports what it cannot measure; playability, feel and emergent design judgement stay with human testers

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns release gates, defect prioritisation and the decision to ship · Duration: 6–10-week build pilot; further 12–22 weeks to studio scale
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, test-automation engineer, build and DevOps engineer; customer QA lead, gameplay engineer, release manager, platform compliance reviewer · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and coverage and escape baseline agreement
2) Build pipeline and defect-workflow integration
3) Test-path authoring and device-matrix configuration
4) Deterministic replay and known-bad fixture setup
5) Build pilot with per-build review and flake governance
6) Stabilisation and handover
